items.label: Keysight Q3 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY is named as one of the three drivers of Keysight's record semiconductor quarter

set.signal: HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY is named by CEO Satish Dhanasekaran as one of the drivers of Keysight's record semiconductor quarter: 'In semiconductor, we delivered another record quarter driven by ongoing capacity expansion for advanced nodes, high-bandwidth memory, and silicon photonics.' EISG President Jason Kary: in semiconductor wafer test 'we're seeing significant capacity expansion there across multiple dimensions, including advanced nodes, memory, silicon photonics', and the forecasts around wafer fab equipment and capital going into those markets 'continues to expand'. CSG President Kailash Narayanan on test intensity: with higher data rates, lower latency and AI that 'needs to be lossless', design margins are shrinking and customers 'can no longer guarantee anything by design'; a compute or switch tray has 'gone from tens to hundreds of IC pinouts'.

items.reason: The verbatim copy has no statement that 'memory fabrics are among the interfaces being characterized'; that clause is not in the source. Speakers now attributed (CEO, Jason Kary, Kailash Narayanan).
items.evidence: Jason Kary: ... semiconductor wafer test, where we're seeing significant capacity expansion there across multiple dimensions, including advanced nodes, memory, silicon photonics.

items.label: Keysight Q3 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Outlook RAISED for Q4 and the full year. Q4 FY2026 revenue guided

set.signal: Outlook RAISED for Q4 and the full year (CEO: 'we're raising our outlook for Q4 and for the full fiscal year'). CFO Neil Dougherty: Q4 FY2026 revenue guided to $1.93-1.95 billion (37% YoY growth at the midpoint) and EPS $3.34-3.40 (approximately 76% YoY growth at the midpoint) on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million, which 'will result in fiscal year 2026 revenue growth of 32% and EPS growth of approximately 60% at the midpoint'. CFO: acquisition integration efforts are 'now largely complete, including systems migrations, one quarter ahead of schedule', so cost synergy realization accelerates in Q4 - 80%-90% of the $100 million in cost synergies realized on a run rate basis exiting the fiscal year, and 'close to 90% of that $100 million realized as we enter next fiscal year'; 'we realized close to $40 million' and, moving from FY2026 to FY2027, 'I'd be thinking on the order of $50 million' incremental. CFO: 'at least as it relates to 2027', he feels confident in the ability to continue to outperform the 40% leverage target, with the caution that 'we did have the one-time tariff impact this year that kind of artificially pulled up 2026 profitability that won't repeat'. CEO: 'We will give you more specific guidance for Q1 when we report in Q4.'

items.reason: Hedge restored: the CFO said integration is 'largely complete', not complete; speakers attributed.
items.evidence: Neil Dougherty: Our integration efforts are now largely complete, including systems migrations, one quarter ahead of schedule.

items.label: Keysight Q3 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Orders $2.091B were a record and the ninth consecutive quarter of CSG order growth

set.signal: Orders of $2.091 billion, up 56% reported (CFO Neil Dougherty). CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: Communications Solutions Group orders grew for the ninth consecutive quarter, establishing a new record, and 'Wireline delivered record orders, more than doubling year-over-year' on AI infrastructure scaling. On aerospace, defense and government the CEO added 'we built backlog in the business', so the segment's revenue is 'a function of supply and supply chain'; CFO: 'demand is not the limiter. We do have some supply chain limitations.' CEO base case: 'orders slightly up from Q3, in line with seasonality, then following that seasonal trend into Q1.' SVP Global Sales Steve Yoon: Q3 was the highest quarter ever for the third consecutive quarter; with the traditional Q4 uplift 'we're confident in delivering another record quarter and surpassing $2 billion for the third consecutive quarter'; the pipeline 'now stands at an all-time high', with the 'highest ever monthly funnel intake just last month' and a record rolling 12 months funnel; nearly 3,000 new customers added year-to-date 'representing more than $100 million of incremental business'; the largest customers are 'performing up high double digits for the year'; Southeast Asia more than doubled and is the fastest-growing region for the quarter and the year. CEO on the Q3 orders: 'There was nothing unusual about the demand. In fact, we saw a conversion of the pipeline in a very orderly fashion. No pull-ins.'
set.figure: Orders $2.091B (+56%); wireline orders more than doubled; Q4 orders base case slightly up from Q3

items.reason: Book-to-bill 'north of 1.1 for two straight quarters' was analyst Matt Niknam's number, not confirmed by management; 'built backlog' was said about the aerospace/defense business; 'in July' was inferred (Steve Yoon said 'just last month'); 'sovereign transceiver restrictions' / 'panic buying' were the analyst's framing.
items.evidence: Matt Niknam: ... but your book to bill has been north of 1.1 for two straight quarters.

items.label: Keysight Q3 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: SUPPLY, NOT DEMAND, IS THE LIMITER.

set.signal: SUPPLY, NOT DEMAND, IS THE LIMITER. CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: traction for the differentiated products and solutions is 'far exceeding our ability to supply at this point'; 'the supply environment is less flexible today than, let's say, a year ago', and Keysight is working with suppliers to deconstrain the supply chain. CFO Neil Dougherty: 'demand is not the limiter. We do have some supply chain limitations.' Three months ago the biggest challenges were internal capacity around ramping some MIPI that had seen 'unprecedented early demand' - 'We have made tremendous progress in that area' - and 'the challenges have shifted more towards incoming parts', with numerous players competing for supply from a similar set of component suppliers; the supply situation 'is likely to be nonlinear and will likely be a governor of our ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters'. CEO: 'Supply chain will remain a governor of near-term revenue'; Keysight has taken an 18-month+ view of supply chain planning to create additional flexibility, 'but those come with a lag' - it will redesign some products on the margin to accommodate second sources and enter into some more longer-term agreements. CEO: 'we remain confident in the guide that we have laid out for Q4.'

items.reason: '(largely fixed)' overstated the CFO, who said 'We have made tremendous progress in that area'; speakers attributed.
items.evidence: Neil Dougherty: ... ramping some MIPI that had seen kind of unprecedented early demand from the marketplace. We have made tremendous progress in that area.

items.label: Keysight Q3 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Optical speed transitions are running CONCURRENTLY rather than sequentially

set.signal: Optical speed transitions are running CONCURRENTLY rather than sequentially - CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: 'pretty unprecedented ... 800G is still sort of the underlying technology, but 1.6T is scaling, and typically that would have been spaced out a little more'. CEO: transceiver manufacturers are rapidly scaling 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers using Keysight's 224G digital communication analyzers (which he calls industry-leading); customers are 'ramping production of 1.6T as we speak right now, and the demand is very strong', and 'in a given quarter like Q4, I can easily see that mix even trend more towards production'. CEO: 'I do know customers are already engaging us on 3.2T' (Keysight did a demo at a conference earlier this year). Optical component ecosystem investment continues to ramp and key players are adopting the lab portfolio, including what Keysight calls 'the industry's first 220 GHz Lightwave Component Analyzer', introduced at OFC this year. CFO Neil Dougherty: the wireline R&D-vs-manufacturing mix, historically about 80/20, shifted to more like 70/30, and over the last couple of quarters 'it's probably more like two-thirds, one-third'.

items.reason: Hedge restored (the CEO 'can easily see' the Q4 mix trend toward production, not an expectation); 'industry's first' attributed as the company's claim; speakers attributed.
items.evidence: Satish Dhanasekaran: So in a given quarter like Q4, I can easily see that mix even trend more towards production.
